text:
Carolina arrives in Calgary as the clear favorite on the numbers. The model has CAR at 3.36 expected goals tonight against 2.67 for CGY. The Hurricanes have controlled 57% of the expected goals at five on five and generate 3.94 expected goals per 60 while allowing 2.51. The Flames sit at 2.98 for and 3.36 against, with a 50% share, and have allowed 5 goals a game while scoring 2. CAR also has the power play edge (1.02 expected goals per game to 0.26 for CGY), and Calgary's 5.1 penalties taken per game keeps feeding it.

Recent form tilts the same way. CAR is 5-0-0 in its last five with 61% of the expected goals, and the Hurricanes have won seven straight, outscoring opponents 32-15, though the model doesn't price the streak itself. CGY is 1-4-0 in its last five at 50%. Calgary is better than its record, with a -21 goal difference against -2.7 expected, but finishing and goaltending have cost it. Carolina is on the second night of a back-to-back after a 3-2 win in Winnipeg, and is missing Taylor Hall and Jordan Staal.

In net, projected starters Brandon Bussi (CAR) and Devin Cooley (CGY) have both struggled this season, at -1.95 and -4.34 goals saved above expected. Last season Cooley was at +17.23 over 31 games, Bussi at +1.15 over 39. Andrei Svechnikov has a 38% chance to score for CAR, and Jackson Blake is at 28%. For CGY, Joel Farabee, Morgan Frost and Matt Coronato each sit at 22 to 23%.
